newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso closes up on intervention.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso closes up on intervention.

text.p: * Central Bank buys between $20 million and $30 million
The Philippine peso ended up on Thursday despite an increase in dollar demand from local oil firms due to the intervention of the Central Bank, traders said.
The peso ended at 26.343 against the dollar from Wednesday's 26.347.
"The Central Bank was there throughout," one trader said. Traders said the Central Bank offered to buy dollars at 26.345 to 26.348.
"Banks unloaded some of their dollars stocks after they saw that the Central Bank was determined to keep a stable exchange rate with the deregulation of the local oil industry," said another trader.
In the afternoon, the Central Bank bought between $20 million and $30 million at 26.341 to 26.343," said a big bank trader.
Philippine oil companies bought $38 million in late trade on Thursday at 26.342 to 26.3427, traders said.
Volume dropped to $106.50 million from the previous $119.7 million. --Manila newsroom (632) 841-89-36, FAX 817-62-67
